lessons.title: Cuttings, Tubers and Lonely Trees: Why Do Plants Reproduce So Differently?

quiz.prompt: Farmers in a Kenyan community plant pieces of cassava stem and sweet potato vines to get new plants, but they buy maize and bean seed before the long rains. Which statement best describes what the farmers are doing?
choices: All crops must be planted as seeds, so the cassava stem must contain hidden seeds
Maize and beans are grown from cuttings, while cassava is grown from seeds
Cassava and sweet potato need a flower on the cutting before they can grow
Some crops are grown from pieces of stem or vine without seeds, while others are grown from seeds
quiz.rationale: The farm scene shows cassava, sugarcane and sweet potato growing from cuttings with no seed, while maize and beans are planted as seeds. The wrong choices reflect the preconception that all plants need seeds or flowers.
quiz.placement: Phase 1 Predict: farm scene chart of cuttings versus seeds and initial model drawing

quiz.prompt: A group examines a ginger piece with a hand lens. It is a thick stem that grows along or just under the soil. It has nodes with small buds along it. Which structure type is it?
choices: Bulb
Runner
Tuber
Rhizome
quiz.rationale: A ginger piece is a rhizome: a thick underground stem with nodes and buds from which new shoots grow.
quiz.placement: Phase 2 Observe: specimen table, ginger rhizome with nodes and buds

quiz.prompt: A teacher cuts an onion bulb in half from top to bottom. What will learners see inside?
choices: A hard seed coat with a tiny embryo inside
A short stem at the base with thick, fleshy leaves that store food
Many thin roots joined to a fruit
A flower that has not yet opened
quiz.rationale: An onion bulb is a short stem (stem plate) surrounded by fleshy leaves that store food. It is not a seed.
quiz.placement: Phase 2 Observe: onion bulb cut open by the teacher

quiz.prompt: A bryophyllum leaf has tiny plantlets growing on it. Where on the leaf do these plantlets grow?
choices: From a flower on the leaf surface
Only from the leaf stalk buried in the soil
From seeds in the middle of the leaf
From the edge (margin) of the leaf
quiz.rationale: Bryophyllum plantlets form along the leaf margin. They grow without seeds or flowers and can fall off and root in the soil.
quiz.placement: Phase 2 Observe: bryophyllum leaf with plantlets on the margin

quiz.prompt: Ferns and mushrooms reproduce by spores (sporulation). Which statement correctly tells a spore apart from a seed?
choices: A spore contains an embryo and a food store, while a seed is a single cell
A spore and a seed are the same thing with different names
A spore is a single cell with no stored food, while a seed contains an embryo and a food store
A spore forms only inside flowers, while a seed forms on leaves
quiz.rationale: Spores are single cells with no stored food. A seed contains an embryo together with stored food. This difference was discussed when the teacher showed bread mould or a fern frond.
quiz.placement: Phase 2 Observe: teacher question 'How is a spore different from a seed?' with bread mould or fern picture

quiz.prompt: A farmer grows a whole field of cassava from cuttings taken from one parent plant. A disease called cassava mosaic attacks, and the parent plant is weak against it. What is most likely to happen to the plants in the field?
choices: Because the plants are identical to the parent, many of them may also be weak against the disease
Each plant is different, so some will always resist the disease
Cuttings do not carry diseases, so the field will be safe
The new plants will become stronger because they have no seeds
quiz.rationale: Growing from cuttings of one parent gives offspring identical to that parent, so they share its weakness. This is a disadvantage of asexual reproduction.
quiz.placement: Phase 3 Explain: Think-Pair-Share on advantages and disadvantages of growing cassava from cuttings

quiz.prompt: A lone avocado tree in a compound is covered in flowers but never sets fruit. After today's lesson on cuttings, tubers, bulbs, rhizomes and runners, what is the best statement about this tree?
choices: It is explained: avocado trees have no bulbs, so they cannot make fruit
It is not explained yet: it is a question for the Driving Question Board and the next lesson on flowers
It is explained: flowers on a tree always make fruit on their own
It is explained: the tree reproduces by runners, so it does not need fruit
quiz.rationale: Today's lesson shows how plants make new plants without seeds. It does not explain why a flowering tree gives no fruit, so this stays an open question on the board for the next lesson.
quiz.placement: Phase 4 DQB: questions about the lone avocado or pawpaw posted under 'With Seeds'

lessons.title: Flower Detectives: Classifying Flowers by Ovary Position, Symmetry, Inflorescence and Sex

quiz.prompt: A learner cuts a Hibiscus flower lengthwise and sees that the ovary sits above the point where the petals attach. How is this ovary described?
choices: Zygomorphic ovary
Unisexual ovary
Superior ovary
Inferior ovary
quiz.rationale: An ovary above the point where the petals attach is superior. An inferior ovary sits below that point, while zygomorphic describes symmetry and unisexual describes whether both male and female parts are present.
quiz.placement: Observe: slicing the flower lengthwise to see whether the ovary sits above (superior) or below (inferior) the point where petals attach

quiz.prompt: A learner cuts a flower in two along several different lines and gets two equal halves every time. What type of symmetry does the flower have?
choices: Unisexual, because the halves are equal
Inferior, because the halves are the same size
Zygomorphic, because it can be cut in more than one way
Actinomorphic, because more than one line gives equal halves
quiz.rationale: A flower is actinomorphic (regular) if more than one line gives equal halves. A zygomorphic flower gives equal halves along only one line.
quiz.placement: Observe: counting petals and sepals and deciding symmetry by cutting the flower along different lines

quiz.prompt: A Bougainvillea branch has small flowers surrounded by showy, colourful parts that look like petals. What are the showy, colourful parts?
choices: Bracts, and the real flowers are the small ones inside them
Stamens, which are brightly coloured to attract insects
Ovaries, which grow outside the flower
Petals, and the small flowers are extra sepals
quiz.rationale: In Bougainvillea the colourful parts are bracts that surround the small true flowers. This is why the 'petals' seen at first are misleading.
quiz.placement: Observe: Bougainvillea station (which parts are the real flowers and which are the colourful bracts)

quiz.prompt: A maize plant has a tassel at the top and a cob with silks lower down. Which statement about the flowers of maize is correct?
choices: The tassel carries female flowers and the silks belong to male flowers
Every maize flower is bisexual, with stamens and carpels together
Male and female flowers are on different maize plants
The tassel carries male flowers and the silks belong to female flowers, both on the same plant
quiz.rationale: Maize has separate unisexual flowers on one plant: the tassel has the male parts (stamens) and the silks are part of the female flowers. This is called monoecious.
quiz.placement: Observe: maize inflorescence station (male tassel and female cob silks on the same plant)

quiz.prompt: A farmer in Kisumu has one pawpaw tree that is covered in flowers every season but never gives fruit. Which explanation is best supported by what we know about flowers?
choices: Fruit forms from petals, and the tree has too few petals
Fruit develops from a fertilised ovary, so if the flowers on the tree lack stamens or carpels, pollen or ovules must come from another tree
Only flowers with an inferior ovary can make fruit
Many flowers always means many fruits, so the tree must be sick
quiz.rationale: Fruit forms from a fertilised ovary, which needs pollen from stamens. If a tree has only flowers of one sex, it needs another tree to supply the missing part. The idea that many flowers mean many fruits is a misconception.
quiz.placement: Explain Part B: CER on classification and the phenomenon (why a lone pawpaw or avocado tree may have many flowers but no fruit)

quiz.prompt: A learner cuts across the ovary of a flower and sees small chambers with tiny round structures attached inside. What is the way these ovules are attached inside the ovary called?
choices: Symmetry
Inflorescence
Placentation
Pollination
quiz.rationale: Placentation is how ovules are attached inside the ovary. Inflorescence is how flowers are arranged on the plant, and pollination is the transfer of pollen.
quiz.placement: Explain Part A: Think-Pair-Share on placentation (counting chambers and seeing how ovules are attached)

quiz.prompt: A group adds an arrow to its model of a flower to show how pollen must move before fruit can form. Which arrow is correct?
choices: From the anther of the stamen to the stigma of the carpel
From the stigma to the anther
From the ovary to the filament
From the petal to the ovary
quiz.rationale: Pollen is made in the anthers (male part) and must reach the stigma (female part) so that the ovary can be fertilised and develop into fruit.
quiz.placement: Model: adding a 'Flower' section with an arrow system showing that fruit needs pollen to reach the ovary

lessons.title: Why Can a Lone Pawpaw Tree Flower Heavily but Never Set Fruit? Adaptations That Prevent Self-Pollination

quiz.prompt: A pawpaw tree stands alone in a compound in Kisumu. It has hundreds of flowers every season but never sets a single fruit. Which explanation is best supported by what we know about pawpaw?
choices: Pawpaw trees are usually either male or female, so a lone tree may have no partner tree to supply pollen or ovules
Pawpaw flowers always pollinate themselves, so the tree must be sick
Pawpaw trees only produce fruit when grown from cuttings, not from seed
The tree has too many flowers, so none can develop into fruit
quiz.rationale: Pawpaw shows dioecy: male and female flowers are on different trees. A lone tree of one sex cannot pollinate itself, so flowers form but no fruit follows.
quiz.placement: Predict: photo of a lone pawpaw/avocado tree covered in flowers with no fruit

quiz.prompt: In a maize plant, the tassels shed their pollen before the silks on the same plant have emerged and are ready to receive pollen. What is this timing adaptation called?
choices: Dioecy
Protandry
Protogyny
Heterostyly
quiz.rationale: Protandry is when the male parts release pollen before the female parts of the same plant are receptive. This reduces self-pollination.
quiz.placement: Station 1 - Timing (protandry/protogyny): maize tassels and silks timeline

quiz.prompt: A 'pin' flower has a long style and short stamens. A 'thrum' flower has a short style and long stamens. How does this arrangement (heterostyly) promote cross-pollination?
choices: The stigma of each flower chemically rejects its own pollen
The anthers and stigma are at different heights, so an insect carries pollen from a flower of one type to the stigma of the other type
The pollen is shed before the stigma is ready
The flowers are on separate trees, so pollen must travel between trees
quiz.rationale: In pin and thrum flowers the anthers and stigma sit at different heights. Pollen from a flower's own anther is poorly placed to reach its own stigma, while an insect moves pollen between the two types.
quiz.placement: Station 2 - Structure (heterostyly): wire/bead pin and thrum flower models

quiz.prompt: Maize has separate male flowers (tassels) and female flowers (cobs with silks) on the same plant. Does this arrangement completely prevent self-pollination?
choices: Yes, because each maize plant is either male or female
Yes, because male and female flowers can never meet
No, because maize flowers have both male and female parts in the same flower
No, pollen from the tassel can still land on silks of the same plant, so self-pollination is only reduced
quiz.rationale: Maize is monoecious: separate flowers on one plant. Pollen can still fall or blow onto silks of the same plant, so self-pollination is reduced but not eliminated. Dioecy, with separate male and female plants as in pawpaw, is different.
quiz.placement: Station 3 - Separate sexes (dioecy): comparison of pawpaw with maize (monoecious)

quiz.prompt: A passion fruit flower has mature pollen and a receptive stigma. Pollen from the same flower lands on its stigma, but the pollen does not germinate and is rejected. Which adaptation is this?
choices: Protandry
Self-incompatibility
Dioecy
Heterostyly
quiz.rationale: In self-incompatibility the stigma recognises and rejects pollen from the same plant, even when both are mature. Timing, height and separate sexes are not involved here.
quiz.placement: Station 4 - Chemistry (self-incompatibility): passion fruit coloured-bead simulation

quiz.prompt: A farmer in Kisii plants cassava cuttings and gets new plants without any flowers or partner plants. Why do cassava cuttings not need a partner?
choices: Cassava cuttings produce pollen that fertilises its own ovules
Cassava trees are male or female, so cuttings take the correct sex
Cassava has self-incompatibility, so it avoids partners
Growing from cuttings is asexual reproduction, so there is no pollination and the new plant is identical to the parent
quiz.rationale: Cuttings grow from a piece of stem, so no pollen, ovule or fertilisation is needed. The new plant is a clone of the parent, so the barriers to self-pollination do not matter.
quiz.placement: Part A - Think-Pair-Share: which adaptation explains the lone pawpaw and why cassava cuttings need no partner

quiz.prompt: Which statement best explains why many flowering plants have adaptations that promote cross-pollination?
choices: Flowers that self-pollinate are weak and always die
Self-pollination never produces seeds in any plant
Cross-pollination mixes the genes of two parents, giving varied offspring that may resist disease better
Cross-pollination produces offspring that are exact copies of the parent
quiz.rationale: Cross-pollination brings together genes from different plants, which gives genetic variation. This is useful to the species, for example varied maize crops resisting disease. It is a problem only for a farmer with a single tree.
quiz.placement: Part B - Claim-Evidence-Reasoning: reasoning that adaptations promote cross-pollination and genetic variation

quiz.prompt: After today's work, a class says they can now explain why a lone tree full of flowers bears no fruit. Which new question follows most logically from their evidence?
choices: Why does a lone tree have flowers but no fruit?
Why can a cassava cutting grow into a whole plant without a partner?
What happens inside the flower after compatible pollen lands on a receptive stigma?
Why are maize tassels and silks on the same plant?
quiz.rationale: The other three questions were already answered by the station evidence. The step after compatible pollen lands on the stigma has not yet been explained, so it is the new question for the next lesson.
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: 'What we figured out' and 'New questions' sticky notes

quiz.prompt: A farmer has one female pawpaw tree. It flowers well but gives no fruit. What should the farmer do to get fruit?
choices: Spray the tree with water so the stigmas can reject their own pollen
Take cuttings from the female tree and plant them next to it
Cut off half of the flowers so the rest can pollinate themselves
Plant a male pawpaw tree nearby so pollen can be carried to the female flowers
quiz.rationale: Pawpaw is dioecy, so female flowers need pollen from a male tree. Cuttings from the female tree would also be female. Pollinating itself is impossible for a female tree.
quiz.placement: Model revision: farmers' choices and the lone pawpaw case (partner tree needed)

lessons.title: Following the Pollen Tube: How Double Fertilisation Explains Why a Lone Pawpaw Flowers but Sets No Fruit

quiz.prompt: A pollen grain lands on the stigma of a compatible flower. Which route do the male nuclei take to reach the egg cell?
choices: The pollen grain mixes with nectar and flows down the stem to the ovule
The pollen grain falls straight through the petals onto the egg cell
The pollen grain stays on the stigma and the egg cell moves up the style to meet it
The pollen grain germinates and a pollen tube grows down the style to the ovary, then into the ovule to the egg cell
quiz.rationale: After landing on the stigma the pollen grain germinates, and the pollen tube carries the male nuclei down the style to the ovary and ovule. Pollen never lands directly on the egg cell.
quiz.placement: Predict: written and drawn prediction of the route of the male cell, using the lone pawpaw and cassava cutting sketch

quiz.prompt: A pollen tube has grown down the style and into the ovary and an ovule. Through which structure does it enter the ovule to reach the embryo sac?
choices: The filament
The petal base
The stigma
The micropyle
quiz.rationale: The pollen tube enters the ovule through a small opening called the micropyle and then releases the sperm nuclei into the embryo sac. The stigma is where pollen lands, at the start of the route.
quiz.placement: Observe: pathway diagram worksheet, animation paused at micropyle entry

quiz.prompt: When a pollen tube reaches the embryo sac, it releases two sperm nuclei. What does each sperm nucleus do?
choices: One sperm nucleus fuses with the tube nucleus, and the other fuses with the egg cell
One sperm nucleus fuses with the egg cell, and the other disappears because it is not needed
One sperm nucleus fuses with the egg cell, and the other fuses with the two polar nuclei
Both sperm nuclei fuse with the egg cell to make a strong zygote
quiz.rationale: Double fertilisation involves two fusions. One sperm nucleus joins the egg cell to form the zygote. The other joins the two polar nuclei to form the endosperm nucleus.
quiz.placement: Observe: animation paused at the two fusions of double fertilisation, and the evidence table

quiz.prompt: A learner says: "Pollination and fertilisation are the same thing." Which statement correctly corrects this learner?
choices: Pollination happens inside the ovule, and fertilisation happens on the stigma
Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma, and fertilisation is the fusion of the sperm nuclei with the egg cell and polar nuclei
Pollination is the fusion of a sperm nucleus with an egg cell, and fertilisation is the landing of pollen on the stigma
Pollination happens only in maize, and fertilisation happens only in beans
quiz.rationale: Pollination is only the transfer of pollen to the stigma. Fertilisation is the later fusion of nuclei inside the embryo sac, after the pollen tube has delivered the sperm nuclei.
quiz.placement: Explain: Think-Pair-Share on double fertilisation, correcting the misconception that pollination is fertilisation

quiz.prompt: A single pawpaw tree in a compound in Kisumu is covered in flowers but sets no fruit. There is no other pawpaw tree nearby. Which explanation is best supported by what happens inside a flower?
choices: The tree has too many flowers, so the pollen is used up before it reaches the stigma
The tree makes seeds without fertilisation, but they fall off before they can be seen
The flowers need to be cut off so that the stem can grow into a new plant
No compatible pollen arrives, so no pollen tube grows, no gametes fuse, and no zygote or endosperm forms, so there is no seed or fruit
quiz.rationale: Fruit and seed formation needs fertilisation. Without compatible pollen there is no pollen tube and no fusion, so no zygote or endosperm forms and the flowers do not set fruit.
quiz.placement: Explain: individual Claim-Evidence-Reasoning paragraph on why a lone pawpaw or avocado tree flowers but sets no fruit

quiz.prompt: In maize, the egg cell, each sperm nucleus and each polar nucleus have 10 chromosomes. One sperm nucleus fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the endosperm nucleus. How many chromosomes does the endosperm nucleus have?
quiz.rationale: The endosperm nucleus is formed from one sperm nucleus and two polar nuclei, which is three nuclei of 10 chromosomes each. 3 × 10 = 30, so the endosperm is triploid. The value 20 is the number in the zygote, which forms from the other fusion.
quiz.placement: Model: pair oral probe 'Why is the endosperm triploid?' and the revised class poster of products of double fertilisation

quiz.prompt: A Kenyan farmer grows cassava from stem cuttings and maize from seeds. Which statement correctly contrasts the two methods?
choices: Cassava cuttings need a compatible partner plant for pollen, while maize seeds do not
Maize grains form without fertilisation, while cassava cuttings form a zygote and an endosperm
Cassava cuttings grow into new plants without any fusion of gametes, while a maize grain forms only after fertilisation of the egg cell and polar nuclei
Both cassava cuttings and maize grains form only after the fusion of gametes
quiz.rationale: A cassava cutting is asexual propagation, so no gametes fuse and the new plant is identical to the parent. A maize grain, with its embryo and endosperm, forms only after double fertilisation.
quiz.placement: End of lesson: revised class model comparing the Asexual branch (cassava cuttings) with the Sexual branch (maize seeds)

lessons.title: Inside the Fruit: Placentation as Evidence of Post-Fertilisation Development

quiz.prompt: After a flower has been fertilised, which part of the flower becomes the fruit and which part becomes the seed?
choices: The ovule becomes the fruit and the ovary becomes the seed
The ovary becomes the fruit and the ovule becomes the seed
The ovary becomes the seed and the stigma becomes the fruit
The petals become the fruit and the ovule becomes the seed
quiz.rationale: After fertilisation the ovules inside the ovary develop into seeds, and the ovary wall develops into the fruit. The other options swap the parts or use parts that wither.
quiz.placement: Predict: learners predict which part of the flower becomes the fruit

quiz.prompt: What is placentation in a fruit?
choices: The way a fruit changes colour and softens as it ripens
The way pollen lands on the stigma of a flower
The number of seeds that a fruit can produce
The way ovules or seeds are attached to the placenta inside the ovary or fruit
quiz.rationale: Placentation is the arrangement of ovules (later seeds) on the placenta inside the ovary. It is not pollination, ripening or seed number, which are common confusions.
quiz.placement: Observe: learners locate the placenta and seed attachment point and record where seeds are attached in a table

quiz.prompt: A learner cuts a tomato across (transverse section). She sees 2 to 3 chambers, and the seeds are attached to a central column where the walls between the chambers meet. Which type of placentation does the tomato show?
choices: Axile
Free-central
Parietal
Marginal
quiz.rationale: Seeds attached to a central axis in an ovary divided into several chambers (locules) is axile placentation, as in tomato and orange. Free-central has a central column without partitions.
quiz.placement: Observe: sectioning tomato and orange (transverse section)

quiz.prompt: A passion fruit is cut across. It has one single chamber and the seeds are attached to the inner wall of the fruit. Which type of placentation is this?
choices: Axile, because the seeds are attached to a central axis
Marginal, because the seeds are attached along one seam
Free-central, because there is a column in the middle
Parietal, because the seeds are attached to the wall of a single chamber
quiz.rationale: Seeds on the wall of a single-chambered ovary show parietal placentation, as in passion fruit and cucumber. Marginal placentation has seeds along only one edge or seam, as in a bean pod.
quiz.placement: Observe: sectioning passion fruit and cucumber (transverse section)

quiz.prompt: A lone pawpaw tree in a compound is covered in flowers but bears no fruit, and there is no other pawpaw tree nearby. Which explanation is best?
choices: The ovules turned into fruit without the ovary, so no seeds could form
The petals normally become the fruit, and they fell off the tree too early
The flowers were not pollinated and fertilised, so the ovules did not become seeds and the ovary did not become a fruit
The tree has the wrong placentation, so the flowers cannot produce fruit
quiz.rationale: Fruit and seeds form only after fertilisation. With no pollen from a partner tree there is no fertilisation, so the ovules and ovary do not develop. Placentation describes seed arrangement, not whether fruit forms.
quiz.placement: Explain: learners explain why a lone avocado or pawpaw with flowers but no pollination from another tree gives no seeds and no fruit

quiz.prompt: A learner says, "A bean pod is not a fruit because it is dry and not sweet like a mango." Which response is correct?
choices: The learner is wrong, because a bean pod is a seed that has grown larger
The learner is wrong, because the bean pod is a dry fruit: it is the developed ovary and it contains the seeds
The learner is right, because the pod is a leaf that protects the seeds
The learner is right, because only sweet and juicy structures are fruits
quiz.rationale: A fruit is a developed ovary containing seeds, whether it is sweet or dry. The bean pod (a legume) is a dry fruit with seeds attached along its seam.
quiz.placement: Explain: teacher corrects the misconception that 'the fruit is only the sweet part' by asking whether a bean pod is a fruit

quiz.prompt: A farmer plants a piece of cassava stem and it grows into a new plant. Which statement correctly describes how this new plant formed?
choices: It formed after the cutting was pollinated by pollen from another cassava plant
It formed because the cutting first made seeds inside a fruit
It formed without flowers, fertilisation or seeds, because the cutting grows directly into a new plant
It formed after double fertilisation inside the cutting
quiz.rationale: Vegetative propagation by cuttings bypasses flowers, pollination, fertilisation and seeds. This is the parallel branch of the class model, separate from the flower to seed to fruit route.
quiz.placement: Model: learners keep the parallel branch of vegetative propagation (cassava, sugarcane, sweet potato cuttings) on the class model

lessons.title: Variation or Copies? Debating the Trade-offs of Sexual and Asexual Reproduction in Kenyan Crops

quiz.prompt: A new fungal disease reaches two farms near Kakamega. Farm A has cassava grown from cuttings taken from one parent plant. Farm B has maize grown from seeds collected from many different plants. What is the most likely result?
choices: Farm A is likely to be badly affected because all its plants are identical, while on Farm B some plants may survive because they differ
Farm A is safe because plants grown from cuttings are stronger than plants grown from seeds
Both farms are affected in the same way because a disease attacks every plant equally
Farm B loses every plant because seed-grown plants are always weaker
quiz.rationale: Cuttings give genetically identical plants, so if one is susceptible all are. Seed-grown maize shows variation, so some plants may resist the disease.
quiz.placement: Predict: two-farm scenario (Farm A cassava cuttings, Farm B maize seeds) near Kakamega

quiz.prompt: In Kisii, banana suckers were taken from one infected plant and planted across a shamba. Banana wilt then spread through almost the whole shamba. Why did it spread so easily?
choices: Bananas must be cross-pollinated, and the pollinators carried the disease
Suckers are genetically identical to the parent, so all the plants are equally susceptible to the disease
The suckers grew from seeds that carried the disease
Suckers show a lot of variation, so the disease could change to attack each plant
quiz.rationale: Suckers are produced by asexual reproduction, so they are clones of the parent. A disease that can infect one plant can infect all of them.
quiz.placement: Observe: case card (1) Banana wilt in Kisii

quiz.prompt: During a drought in a field in Machakos, some seed-grown maize plants survived while many others died. What best explains why some plants survived?
choices: All the maize plants were identical, so the survivors were just lucky
Maize reproduces asexually, so the survivors were clones of a drought-resistant parent
Sexual reproduction produced seeds with different gene combinations, so some plants could tolerate drought
The drought changed the genes of every plant so that they could survive
quiz.rationale: Meiosis and fertilisation mix genes, so seed-grown plants differ from each other. Some of these differences can help a plant survive when conditions change.
quiz.placement: Observe: case card (2) Maize seed variation in a drought-hit field in Machakos

quiz.prompt: A farmer in Busia has one cassava plant with a high yield and a sweet taste. Why is it a good choice to plant cuttings from this plant?
choices: The cuttings will give new varieties with different tastes, so the farmer can choose the best one
The cuttings need another cassava variety nearby for pollination before they can grow
The cuttings will be resistant to every disease because they come from a healthy plant
The cuttings quickly and cheaply give many plants that are identical to the parent, with the same high yield and taste
quiz.rationale: Asexual reproduction gives fast, cheap, identical copies (clones) without a partner. This keeps the useful features of the parent.
quiz.placement: Observe: case card (3) Cassava cuttings in Busia

quiz.prompt: A single avocado tree in a compound is covered in flowers every season but never sets fruit. No other avocado tree grows nearby. What is the best explanation?
choices: Flowers cannot form fruit unless the plant is grown from seed
The tree has too many flowers and uses up all its energy before fruits can form
Fruit and seeds need pollination and fertilisation, and the avocado often needs pollen from another tree, which is not available here
Avocado reproduces only by cuttings, so flowers cannot make fruit
quiz.rationale: Fruits develop after pollination and fertilisation. Many avocado and pawpaw trees need cross-pollination, so a lone tree may flower but not fruit.
quiz.placement: Explain: 'why a stem cutting grows with no flower while a lone avocado tree cannot set fruit'

quiz.prompt: In the class debate on the motion 'A Kenyan farmer should plant only cuttings, never seeds', which is the strongest point for the side that opposes the motion?
choices: Seeds give variation, so some plants may survive a disease or drought, and seeds can also spread to new areas
Cuttings always need a partner plant for pollination, but seeds do not
Seeds give plants that are identical to the parent, so the farmer keeps the same yield
Cuttings are slower than seeds, so farmers lose time
quiz.rationale: Seeds come from sexual reproduction, which gives variation and helps dispersal. Variation means a single disease or drought is less likely to destroy all the plants. The other choices are wrong because cuttings are fast, need no partner, and seeds do not give identical offspring.
quiz.placement: Explain: structured debate on 'A Kenyan farmer should plant only cuttings, never seeds'

quiz.prompt: Which statement is the best conclusion about sexual and asexual reproduction in plants?
choices: Neither is better in all conditions: asexual gives fast identical copies, sexual gives variation, and the best choice depends on the crop and the environment
Both give identical offspring, so the choice does not matter to the farmer
Sexual reproduction is always better because it gives variation
Asexual reproduction is always better because it is faster and needs no partner
quiz.rationale: Cloning is useful for quickly copying a good variety but is risky if a disease arrives. Variation from seeds helps survival when conditions change. The better strategy depends on the situation.
quiz.placement: End of lesson: revised class model and exit ticket on advising a farmer about cassava and beans

lessons.title: Putting the Evidence Together: Why Cassava Cuttings Need No Seeds but Lone Pawpaw and Avocado Trees Need a Partner

quiz.prompt: A farmer in Kisumu plants a piece of cassava stem in the soil. It grows into a whole new plant without any flower, pollen or seed. Which statement best explains this?
choices: The stem cutting must first be pollinated by insects before it can grow
The cutting grows only because it has a flower that is too small to see
New roots and shoots grow from the stem tissue of the parent, so no flowers or fertilisation are needed
The cutting is really a seed that is hidden inside the stem
quiz.rationale: Vegetative propagation (asexual reproduction) grows a new plant from a part of the parent, so no gametes, pollination or fertilisation are needed. A cutting is not a seed.
quiz.placement: Predict: why does a cassava cutting not need flower parts?

quiz.prompt: In a hibiscus flower, the anthers release their pollen before the stigma of the same flower is ready to receive it. What is this feature called, and what does it do?
choices: Dioecy: male and female flowers are on separate plants
Protandry: the timing difference makes self-pollination less likely
Monoecy: male and female flowers are on the same plant
Herkogamy: the stigma and anthers are at different heights
quiz.rationale: Protandry means the anthers mature and release pollen before the stigma is receptive. This hinders self-pollination. Herkogamy is a difference in height, not in timing.
quiz.placement: Observe: hibiscus flower dissection, features that hinder self-pollination

quiz.prompt: A maize plant has male tassels at the top and female cobs with silk lower down on the same plant. Which description is correct?
choices: It is protandrous, because the cob grows from the tassel
It is self-incompatible, because it has no male parts
It is monoecious, because separate male and female flowers grow on the same plant
It is dioecious, because it has male and female parts on separate plants
quiz.rationale: Monoecious plants such as maize have separate male flowers (tassels) and female flowers (cobs) on the same plant. Pollen moves by wind from the tassel to the silk. Dioecious plants have them on separate plants.
quiz.placement: Observe: labelled chart comparing pawpaw (dioecious) and maize (monoecious)

quiz.prompt: During double fertilisation in a flowering plant, two sperm nuclei from the pollen tube enter the ovule. What does each one do?
choices: One forms the seed coat and the other forms the fruit wall
Both fuse with the egg to form two embryos
One fuses with the egg to form the endosperm, and the other fuses with the polar nuclei to form the zygote
One fuses with the egg to form the zygote, and the other fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm
quiz.rationale: One sperm nucleus fuses with the egg to form the zygote (the future embryo). The other fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm, the food store in seeds such as maize.
quiz.placement: Observe: pre-downloaded animation of double fertilisation, paused at pollen tube growth

quiz.prompt: A bean pod is opened and the seeds are found attached in a row along one edge of the pod. What type of placentation is this?
choices: Parietal placentation
Free-central placentation
Axile placentation
Marginal placentation
quiz.rationale: In beans, ovules attach along one edge (suture) of the single-chambered ovary, which is marginal placentation. Axile is seen in tomato, and parietal in passion fruit.
quiz.placement: Explain: Think-Pair-Share on placentation of tomato, passion fruit and bean pod

quiz.prompt: After pollination and fertilisation in a tomato flower, which part of the flower develops into the fruit and which part develops into the seeds?
choices: The ovary becomes the fruit and the ovules become the seeds
The ovules become the fruit and the ovary becomes the seeds
The petals become the fruit and the anthers become the seeds
The stigma becomes the fruit and the style becomes the seeds
quiz.rationale: The fertilised ovary develops into the fruit, and the fertilised ovules inside it develop into seeds. This is why fruit forms only after pollination and fertilisation.
quiz.placement: Explain: CER statement for classifying a fruit

quiz.prompt: A farmer in Kericho plants a whole field with cassava cuttings taken from one parent plant. A disease that attacks this variety arrives. Why is the whole field at high risk?
choices: Cuttings produce seeds that carry the disease
Cuttings from one parent are genetically identical, so they all lack resistance to the disease
Cuttings need pollinators, and the disease kills them
Cuttings always grow more slowly than seeds, so they are weak
quiz.rationale: Asexual reproduction produces offspring identical to the parent with no variation, so a disease can spread through all of them. Sexual reproduction gives variation, so some plants may resist the disease.
quiz.placement: Explain: comparing advantages and disadvantages of cuttings and seeds

quiz.prompt: A lone avocado tree in a compound in Kiambu is covered in flowers every year but never sets fruit. Which explanation best uses what we know about barriers to self-pollination?
choices: Flowers are only for decoration, so they never lead to fruit
Avocado trees can only be grown from cuttings, so they cannot form fruit
Its flowers cannot be fertilised by its own pollen (self-incompatibility), so it needs pollen from another avocado tree
The tree has too many petals, which stop the ovary from growing
quiz.rationale: Barriers such as self-incompatibility and flowers maturing at different times stop a lone tree from fertilising itself. Pollen from a second tree is needed before the ovary can develop into fruit.
quiz.placement: DQB: posting an evidence-based answer to why the lone pawpaw or avocado has flowers but no fruit

lessons.title: Final Explanation: Why Cassava Cuttings Grow Without Seeds but a Lone Pawpaw Needs a Partner Tree

quiz.prompt: A lone avocado tree in a Nairobi compound is covered in flowers but sets no fruit. A second avocado tree is planted 10 m away. Which outcome is most likely once both trees flower?
choices: The second tree gives the first tree extra water, so its flowers will make fruit
The first tree will start making fruit from its flowers by mitosis alone
The two trees join their roots, so no pollen is needed to make fruit
Pollen can be carried between the two trees, so cross-pollination and fertilisation can happen and fruit can form
quiz.rationale: A lone tree may fail to fruit because of barriers to self-pollination. A second tree supplies compatible pollen, so cross-pollination, fertilisation and fruit development can follow.
quiz.placement: Index card prediction: lone avocado in a Nairobi compound and a second avocado tree 10 m away

quiz.prompt: A farmer in Kisumu plants a cassava stem cutting. It grows roots and shoots without any flower or pollen. Which statement explains this correctly?
choices: The cutting needs pollen from another cassava plant before it can grow roots
The cutting is a type of seed, so it grows like a seed
Cells in the stem divide by meiosis, so the new plant is different from the parent
Cells in the stem divide by mitosis to form roots and shoots, so the new plant is a clone of the parent
quiz.rationale: Vegetative propagation uses mitosis in vegetative tissue. No gametes are involved, so the offspring is genetically identical to the parent.
quiz.placement: Station A: vegetative propagation charts and photos of cassava, sugarcane and sweet potato cuttings

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a feature that hinders self-pollination in flowering plants?
choices: Anthers and stigma of the same flower ripen at the same time and touch each other
The flower produces a lot of nectar
The flower has a large ovary with many ovules
The stigma of a hibiscus flower matures at a different time from its anthers
quiz.rationale: Different times of maturity of anthers and stigma (dichogamy) make it hard for a flower to pollinate itself. Nectar and a large ovary do not prevent self-pollination.
quiz.placement: Station B: labelled flower diagrams and classification tables, including features that hinder self-pollination

quiz.prompt: During double fertilisation in a flowering plant such as maize, what happens to the two sperm nuclei from the pollen tube?
choices: One sperm nucleus forms the seed coat, and the other forms the fruit wall
One sperm nucleus fuses with the egg cell to form the zygote, and the other fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm
Both sperm nuclei fuse with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm
Both sperm nuclei fuse with the egg cell to form two zygotes
quiz.rationale: One sperm nucleus fertilises the egg to make the diploid zygote. The second joins the polar nuclei to make the endosperm, which feeds the embryo.
quiz.placement: Station C: double fertilisation animation screenshots and group summary of zygote and endosperm formation

quiz.prompt: A learner cuts open a tomato fruit and finds small seeds inside. Which statement about how the fruit and seeds formed is correct?
choices: The petals became the fruit and the anthers became the seeds
The ovule became the fruit and the ovary became the seeds
The whole flower became the fruit and the seeds came from the stigma
The ovary became the fruit and the ovules became the seeds
quiz.rationale: After fertilisation, ovules develop into seeds and the ovary wall develops into the fruit.
quiz.placement: Station D: fruit sections of tomato, passion fruit and bean pod with placentation and fruit type classification

quiz.prompt: A student looks at a pawpaw flower and sees pollen grains on the stigma. Which conclusion is correct?
choices: Neither pollination nor fertilisation can happen without a second tree
Pollination and fertilisation mean the same thing, so the fruit will form
Pollination has happened, but fertilisation has not necessarily happened yet
Fertilisation has definitely happened, because pollen is on the stigma
quiz.rationale: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma. Fertilisation happens later, when the male gamete fuses with the egg, and only if the pollen is compatible and a pollen tube grows.
quiz.placement: Sorting DQB sticky notes into 'Answered', 'Partly answered' and 'New question', including unresolved confusion between pollination and fertilisation

quiz.prompt: A sugarcane farmer in Mumias plants setts (stem pieces) instead of seeds. What is an advantage and a disadvantage of this method?
choices: Advantage: it needs double fertilisation. Disadvantage: it makes fewer plants
Advantage: the crop grows fast and is uniform. Disadvantage: the plants are clones, so a disease can spread to all of them
Advantage: it needs pollen from another farm. Disadvantage: it makes the plants different from each other
Advantage: it creates a lot of genetic variation. Disadvantage: it needs pollinators
quiz.rationale: Setts produce clones by mitosis. This gives fast, uniform crops, but the lack of variation means disease can affect all plants.
quiz.placement: Final model and unit assessment tasks: advantages and disadvantages of asexual and sexual reproduction
